items.title: Kapanan kitapçı
items.titleEn: The Bookshop That Would Not Close
items.text: Nevzat's bookshop has been closing for eleven years. He announced it first in a newspaper, then on a sign in the window, then again at his sixtieth birthday. Every time, something stopped him. Once a customer bought two hundred books in a single week. Once a school started sending its students on Friday afternoons. Once his daughter, who lives abroad, sent money without being asked and told him to use it however he wanted. The truth, which he admits when the shop is empty, is that the accounts have never worked. He sells about thirty books a week in a street where the rent rises every year. He also says, without any sense that the two ideas are in conflict, that he has no intention of closing before he is eighty.

questions.q: How long has the shop been closing?
questions.note: "Nevzat's bookshop has been closing for eleven years."

questions.q: What did his daughter do?
questions.note: "His daughter... sent money without being asked."

questions.q: What does he admit when the shop is empty?
questions.note: "The accounts have never worked."

questions.q: How many books does he sell a week?
questions.note: "He sells about thirty books a week."

questions.q: What does he say about the future?
options: He will not close before he is eighty
He will sell it to his daughter
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Gönüllü arama ekibi
items.text: A search team in the mountains has forty members and none of them is paid. They train two weekends a month in weather that most people would avoid on purpose. In a normal year they are called out eleven or twelve times. Two of those calls end badly, and the team leader says this is the part nobody prepares you for. What surprises new members most is how much of the work is waiting. They sit in a cold room for six hours while somebody with a map decides where to look, and then they walk for four hours and find nothing, and then they go home. The leader tells every new volunteer the same thing on the first day: if you are joining for the rescue, you will leave within a year. If you are joining for the waiting, you will stay.

questions.q: How often does the team train?
questions.note: "They train two weekends a month."

questions.q: How many calls end badly in a normal year?
questions.note: "Two of those calls end badly."

questions.q: What surprises new members most?
options: How much of the work is waiting
questions.note: "How much of the work is waiting."

questions.q: What often happens after four hours of walking?
options: They find nothing and go home
questions.note: "They walk for four hours and find nothing, and then they go home."

questions.q: What does the leader tell new volunteers?
options: Those who join for the rescue leave within a year
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Otuz yaşında üniversite
items.text: Hande started university at thirty after eleven years of full-time work. She expected the studying to be the hard part. It was not. The hard part was sitting in a room where everybody else was nineteen and had never had to explain a late payment to anybody. In the first month she felt like a visitor. Then a lecturer asked the class a question about how companies actually make decisions, and Hande realized she was the only person in the room who had watched it happen. She answered, and after that the age difference stopped feeling like a problem. Her marks are good but not the best. She says the useful thing she gained was not the degree but the discovery that eleven years of ordinary work had taught her more than she had ever given herself credit for.

questions.q: What did Hande expect to be hard?
questions.note: "She expected the studying to be the hard part."

questions.q: What was actually hard?
questions.note: "The hard part was sitting in a room where everybody else was nineteen."

questions.q: What changed things?
options: A question about how companies decide
questions.note: "A lecturer asked the class a question about how companies actually make decisions."

questions.q: How are her marks?
questions.note: "Her marks are good but not the best."

questions.q: What does she say she gained?
options: The discovery that her work had taught her a lot
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Apartman toplantısı
items.text: Eighteen flats, one broken roof, and a meeting that lasted three hours. The repair would cost each flat about two months of rent, and the people on the ground floor pointed out, correctly, that water was not coming into their homes. The people on the top floor pointed out, also correctly, that a roof protects the whole building. For two hours nobody moved. Then a woman from the second floor said something simple: whoever sells first will find that no buyer wants a building with a broken roof, and that includes the ground floor. The room went quiet. The vote passed fifteen to three. The repair took five weeks. Nobody on the ground floor has ever said the woman was right, and everybody knows she was.

questions.q: How long did the meeting last?
questions.note: "A meeting that lasted three hours."

questions.q: What did the ground-floor people point out?
options: Water was not coming into their homes
questions.note: "Water was not coming into their homes."

questions.q: What argument changed the room?
options: No buyer wants a building with a broken roof
The top floor would pay more
questions.note: "Whoever sells first will find that no buyer wants a building with a broken roof."

questions.q: What was the result of the vote?
questions.note: "The vote passed fifteen to three."

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
options: They know she was right but will not say it
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Sessiz saat
items.text: A supermarket chain started a quiet hour on Tuesday mornings. Between nine and ten the music is off, the lights are lower, and the machines at the checkout do not beep. It was designed for customers who find noise difficult, and for a while that is who came. Then something else happened. Older shoppers started arriving at five to nine. Parents with small children discovered the shop was easier without the noise. Staff reported that they finished their shifts less tired. The company measured sales and found that the quiet hour sells slightly less per customer but that Tuesday as a whole is now busier. Twelve other branches have copied it. The manager who suggested it says the interesting part is that nobody had ever asked whether the music was helping in the first place.

questions.q: When is the quiet hour?
questions.note: "A quiet hour on Tuesday mornings."

questions.q: Who was it designed for?
questions.note: "It was designed for customers who find noise difficult."

questions.q: What did the staff report?
options: They finished their shifts less tired
questions.note: "Staff reported that they finished their shifts less tired."

questions.q: What did the sales figures show?
options: Less per customer but a busier Tuesday
questions.note: "Sells slightly less per customer but... Tuesday as a whole is now busier."

questions.q: What does the manager find interesting?
options: Nobody had asked if the music helped
questions.note: Son cümle.
